requirements.requirement: SSH allowed from any address on node1
requirements.summary: public zone has ssh service enabled with no source restriction on node1; SSH connectivity to node1 verified from both node2 and node3, both before and after all node reboots.

requirements.requirement: TCP port 9000 allowed only from node2
requirements.summary: Dedicated source-based zone 'node2-9000' (source=10.100.190.11/32) opens 9000/tcp; a temp listener on node1:9000 was reached with HTTP 200 from node2 both pre- and post-reboot, and iptables output confirms node2 traffic is routed into an accept path via INPUT_ZONES_SOURCE.

requirements.requirement: TCP port 9000 rejected from node3 and everywhere else
requirements.summary: public zone carries a rich-rule 'reject' for tcp/9000 with no source qualifier, matched by iptables REJECT --reject-with icmp-port-unreachable; curl from node3 to node1:9000 returned connection-refused (rc=7) both pre- and post-reboot. Only node2 and node3 were available to test as 'everywhere else' given the 3-node topology, which is an adequate proxy since the rule itself carries no source qualifier.

requirements.requirement: Firewall configuration is persistent across reboot
requirements.summary: Permanent XML zone files on disk match runtime config; node1 was rebooted (boot_id 738d0aac...->d5df004c...) and firewalld came back active with the same node2-9000 zone, port, and public-zone reject rich-rule intact, and functional retest after all three node reboots still showed node2 allowed (200) and node3 rejected (refused).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1
requirements.summary: Pre-restart healthy baseline (boot id, firewalld active, zones) captured, reboot acknowledged via dropped SSH connection, post-restart probe succeeded with a different boot id, and firewalld/rules were confirmed recovered; consistent with fixed after-executor boot-identity snapshot.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node2
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline boot id and sshd-active state captured, reboot acknowledged, post-restart probe succeeded with a changed boot id, sshd active, and cross-node SSH/port-9000 reachability to node1 confirmed; consistent with fixed after-executor snapshot.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node3
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline boot id and sshd-active state captured, reboot acknowledged, post-restart probe succeeded with a changed boot id, sshd active, and SSH reachability to node1 confirmed; consistent with fixed after-executor snapshot.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct, bounded evidence: node1's public zone allows SSH from any source, a dedicated source-scoped zone restricts TCP/9000 to node2 only, a public-zone reject rich-rule blocks 9000 from node3 and all other sources, and the configuration is confirmed persistent because node1's own reboot (with a changed boot id) came back with the identical zones/rules and functional test results (node2 allowed, node3 refused) held both before and after all three nodes were rebooted. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also completed correctly for all three nodes, each showing a pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, a changed post-restart boot id, and recovered service/connectivity state, consistent with the fixed after-executor snapshots.
limitations: Only node2 and node3 were available as test sources given the 3-node topology, so 'everywhere else' for the reject rule was validated via node3 plus the source-agnostic nature of the rich-rule rather than an arbitrary external address.
Minor leftover temp/log files (e.g., /tmp/reboot.log, /tmp/listener9000.log, /tmp/final9000.log, /tmp/x.log) were not cleaned up on the managed nodes after testing/reboots.
The purpose of the node2-local SimpleHTTPServer listener (cmd-e34f2e81143d4388) is not clearly tied to node1 verification and could not be fully explained from the trace.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands directly served configuration, diagnosis, or bounded verification purposes and were reverted where temporary (test listeners on node1 port 9000 were started for functional checks and then killed in cmd-63355ee1bb204ce5/cmd-55bbd4c65f114ba3/cmd-8af69bfb18334c94). One diagnostic experiment (cmd-967714846bcc42c3) attempted an unsupported 'priority' rich-rule attribute, which failed immediately with INVALID_RULE and was corrected in the very next command (cmd-3904c42c867d4caf) that established the final working zone design — this is a normal iterative-correction step, not an unwanted mutation, though it briefly left port 9000 without an explicit rule between the two commands. A command on node2 (cmd-e34f2e81143d4388) started a SimpleHTTPServer listener on node2 itself, which was not clearly connected to any node1 verification step and was later killed (cmd-bdda1b8b0d3f4fa4); its purpose is unclear from the trace. Minor residue: log files (/tmp/reboot.log on all three nodes, /tmp/listener9000.log and /tmp/final9000.log on node1, /tmp/x.log on node2) were left behind by the reboot and test-listener commands and were not cleaned up, confirmed present in the after-executor snapshot.
